plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid half of your value. This is because bidding higher risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing the item to someone who values it more. In this case, my value is $31, so half of that is $15.50. This strategy aims to win only when my valuation exceeds others' enough to justify the cost.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bidders is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win with high probability and avoid overpaying, I will bid slightly above this, but considering my value of 46, I don’t want to bid too high.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value. However, a slight underbid is optimal to avoid overpaying. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value, anticipating others will do the same. Bidding $34.50 aims to win against bids likely clustered below $35 while minimizing the payment if I win.
